title: Neuroblastoma
subtitle: StewardMD ONCOTREE Navigator (NCCN Guidelines Version 2.2026)
provenanceNote: NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) Pediatric Neuroblastoma Version 2.2026 clinical navigator for Neuroblastoma. Covers complete clinical algorithm: Diagnostic Workup (urine HVA/VMA, primary CT/MRI with IDRF assessment, 123I-MIBG or FDG-PET staging, bilateral marrow, INPC Shimada histology, MYCN/1p/11q/ALK biology) -> INRG Risk Stratification (Low vs Intermediate vs High vs Relapsed/Refractory) -> Low-Risk surgery/observation -> Intermediate-Risk moderate chemotherapy per COG ANBL0531 -> High-Risk intensive 3-phase multimodality per COG ANBL0032/ANBL1531 with ASCR, RT, and anti-GD2 maintenance -> Relapsed/Refractory chemoimmunotherapy D-I/T or 131I-MIBG or Lorlatinib. DRAFT - clinical decision support; physician decides and dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
sourceNote: Structured in accordance with NCCN Clinical Practice Guidelines in Oncology (NCCN Guidelines) for Pediatric Neuroblastoma Version 2.2026.

a.text: INRGSS stages disease by pre-treatment imaging: L1 is localized tumor without Image-Defined Risk Factors (IDRFs); L2 is locoregional tumor with one or more IDRFs; M is distant metastatic disease; MS is metastatic disease in infants with spread limited to skin, liver, and marrow (<10% involvement). IDRFs include vascular encasement, intraspinal extension, and infiltration of adjacent organs.

b.text: MYCN amplification by FISH or NGS is the dominant adverse biologic driver: any MYCN-amplified tumor is high-risk regardless of stage, age, or histology. Segmental chromosomal alterations (1p loss, 11q loss, 17q gain) and unfavorable INPC/Shimada histology further refine risk within non-MYCN groups.

c.text: COG ANBL0531 established risk-adapted moderate-intensity chemotherapy (Carboplatin, Etoposide, Cyclophosphamide, Doxorubicin) x 2-8 cycles with delayed resection for intermediate-risk neuroblastoma, achieving 3-year EFS above 85-90% while limiting cumulative toxicity.

d.text: COG ANBL0032 established post-consolidation Dinutuximab plus GM-CSF plus Isotretinoin as standard maintenance for high-risk neuroblastoma after induction, ASCR, and radiotherapy, with significant EFS and OS improvement over isotretinoin alone.

e.text: COG ANBL1221 established Dinutuximab plus Irinotecan plus Temozolomide (D-I/T) as active chemoimmunotherapy for relapsed or refractory neuroblastoma; 131I-MIBG therapy and the ALK inhibitor Lorlatinib are active alternatives for MIBG-avid and ALK-aberrant disease respectively.

nodes.name: Diagnostic Workup
nodes.title: Neuroblastoma: Diagnostic Workup Checklist
nodes.description: Step 1: Complete the diagnostic workup before INRG risk stratification. Confirm catecholamine secretion, define local IDRF status, stage metastatic extent, and establish histology plus mandatory molecular biology.
bullets: Urine catecholamine metabolites: quantitative spot or 24-hour urine homovanillic acid (HVA) and vanillylmandelic acid (VMA); elevated HVA/VMA supports sympathetic neural crest origin and provides a baseline disease marker.

Primary site cross-sectional imaging: contrast-enhanced CT or MRI of the primary site (neck, chest, abdomen, or pelvis) to measure tumor dimensions and determine Image-Defined Risk Factors (IDRFs) such as vascular encasement, intraspinal extension, and adjacent organ infiltration.

Metastatic staging: 123I-MIBG scintigraphy with thyroid protection by potassium iodide or SSKI before tracer administration; use 18F-FDG-PET/CT for MIBG-nonavid tumors or when MIBG is unavailable; add bilateral assessment of cortical bone and soft tissue sites.

Bilateral bone marrow aspirates and core biopsies for microscopic tumor infiltration: bilateral posterior iliac crest sampling with morphology plus immunohistochemistry to detect marrow involvement that upstages disease to M or MS.

Tumor histology: International Neuroblastoma Pathology Classification (INPC, Shimada system) evaluation with favorable vs unfavorable histology assignment, Schwannian stroma content (stroma-rich vs stroma-poor), differentiation grade, and Mitosis-Karyorrhexis Index (MKI: low, intermediate, or high).

Molecular biology: MYCN amplification status by FISH or NGS (mandatory for every case); segmental chromosomal alterations including 1p loss and 11q loss; ALK mutation and amplification testing to guide risk assignment and Lorlatinib eligibility.

options.label: Workup Complete - Proceed to INRG Risk Stratification

nodes.name: INRG Risk Stratification
nodes.title: Neuroblastoma: INRG Risk Stratification
nodes.description: Workup complete. Assign INRG risk from stage (L1/L2/M/MS), age, MYCN status, histology, and segmental biology; risk selects the low, intermediate, high, or relapsed treatment pathway.
bullets: Low risk: INRGSS L1 without IDRFs and non-MYCN-amplified, or asymptomatic infant stage MS/4S without organ compromise; favorable biology with expected 5-year OS above 95% on surgery or observation alone.

Intermediate risk: INRGSS L2 with IDRFs and non-MYCN-amplified, or infants under 18 months with stage M non-MYCN disease; requires moderate-intensity chemotherapy plus delayed resection per COG ANBL0531.

High risk: any MYCN-amplified tumor at any stage and any age, or stage M disease at age 18 months or older, or 12-18 month stage M with unfavorable features (diploidy, 1p/11q aberration, or unfavorable histology); requires intensive 3-phase multimodality therapy.

Relapsed or refractory: prior progression, inadequate response, or recurrence after completed therapy; route to chemoimmunotherapy, 131I-MIBG, or ALK-directed therapy rather than frontline risk pathways.

nodes.name: Low-Risk Treatment
nodes.title: Low-Risk Neuroblastoma: Resection or Observation
nodes.description: Definitive management for low-risk neuroblastoma: surgical resection or active observation with chemotherapy reserved strictly for threatening symptoms.
bullets: Complete or partial surgical resection of the primary tumor when excision is feasible without mutilation: L1 tumors without IDRFs undergo upfront resection with negative-margin intent; document residual disease and IDRF resolution postoperatively.

Active observation alone for asymptomatic perinatal adrenal neuroblastoma (small suprarenal mass in infants under 6 months) and for asymptomatic infant stage MS/4S without liver compromise, respiratory distress, or coagulopathy; serial ultrasound, urine HVA/VMA, and physical examination every 3-6 weeks initially.

Low-dose chemotherapy reserved strictly for symptomatic life- or organ-threatening complications (airway compression, spinal cord compression, bowel or bladder obstruction, massive hepatomegaly with respiratory compromise, or Kasabach-Merritt-like coagulopathy): Carboplatin plus Etoposide per infant dosing with weight-based adjustments.

COG low-risk cohort evidence: surgery alone or observation achieves 5-year overall survival above 95% for L1 non-MYCN and asymptomatic MS disease; avoid overtreatment because late effects exceed disease risk in this group.

Surveillance after resection or during observation: cross-sectional imaging of the primary bed, urine catecholamines, and MIBG only if initially avid; escalate to the intermediate-risk pathway on symptomatic progression or unfavorable biology revision. Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Surgical Resection Alone or Active Observation (OS >95%)

nodes.name: Intermediate-Risk Treatment
nodes.title: Intermediate-Risk Neuroblastoma: Moderate Chemotherapy Plus Delayed Resection
nodes.description: Risk-adapted moderate-intensity chemotherapy followed by delayed resection for intermediate-risk neuroblastoma, with radiotherapy reserved for refractory progression.
bullets: Risk-adapted moderate-intensity chemotherapy per COG ANBL0531: 2 to 8 cycles of Carboplatin 560 mg/m2 IV day 1, Etoposide 120 mg/m2/d IV days 1-3, Cyclophosphamide 1000 mg/m2 IV day 1, and Doxorubicin 30 mg/m2 IV day 1, given every 21 days with cycle number set by response and biology (favorable biology: 2-4 cycles; unfavorable features: up to 8 cycles).

Delayed surgical resection of the residual primary tumor after 2-4 cycles once IDRFs regress and the tumor is resectable without mutilation; attempt gross total resection greater than 90% while preserving encased vessels and organs.

Radiotherapy reserved only for persistent progressive disease unresponsive to chemotherapy and surgery: limited-field external beam RT per pediatric radiation oncology planning; routine adjuvant RT is not indicated in intermediate-risk disease.

COG ANBL0531 trial evidence: risk-adapted moderate chemotherapy with surgery achieved 3-year event-free survival above 85-90% for L2 non-MYCN and infant stage M non-MYCN cohorts with reduced cumulative anthracycline and alkylator exposure versus high-risk regimens.

Monitoring: audiometry (carboplatin ototoxicity), echocardiography (doxorubicin cardiotoxicity), CBC with growth-factor support per cycle, and urine HVA/VMA plus cross-sectional imaging every 2 cycles; stem-cell harvest is not required. Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Moderate Chemotherapy (Carbo/Etop/Cyclo/Dox) x 2-8 cycles + Delayed Resection

nodes.name: High-Risk Treatment
nodes.title: High-Risk Neuroblastoma: Intensive 3-Phase Multimodality Therapy
nodes.description: Intensive 3-phase multimodality therapy for high-risk neuroblastoma: dose-intensive induction with resection, myeloablative consolidation with ASCR plus RT, then anti-GD2 post-consolidation maintenance.
bullets: Phase 1 (Induction): 5-6 cycles of dose-intensive chemotherapy per COG ANBL0032/ANBL1531: Cyclophosphamide 4000 mg/m2 with Mesna plus Vincristine 1.5 mg/m2 (cap 2 mg) plus Doxorubicin 75 mg/m2 alternating every 21 days with Cisplatin 200 mg/m2 over 4 days plus Etoposide 600 mg/m2 over 4 days; perform gross total tumor resection after 4-5 cycles when IDRFs permit; collect peripheral blood stem cells after cycle 2-3.

Phase 2 (Consolidation): single or tandem high-dose myeloablative chemotherapy with Autologous Stem Cell Rescue (ASCR): Carboplatin 425 mg/m2/d plus Etoposide 338 mg/m2/d plus Melphalan 70 mg/m2/d with stem-cell infusion, followed by 21.6 Gy external beam radiotherapy in 12 fractions of 1.8 Gy to the pre-operative primary bed and to MIBG-avid metastatic sites persisting after induction.

Phase 3 (Post-Consolidation Maintenance): anti-GD2 immunotherapy per COG ANBL0032: Dinutuximab 17.5 mg/m2/d IV over 10-20 hours on days 1-4 of each 28-day cycle x 5 cycles with GM-CSF 250 mcg/m2/d subcutaneously days 1-14 plus Isotretinoin (13-cis-retinoic acid) 160 mg/m2/d PO divided BID on days 1-14 every 28 days x 6 cycles; manage Dinutuximab neuropathic pain, capillary leak, and hypersensitivity with prehydration, opioids, and infusion-rate control.

ALK-aberrant tumors: add the ALK inhibitor Lorlatinib 95 mg/m2 PO once daily (adult equivalent 100 mg daily) concurrently with maintenance and continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity, per COG ANBL1531 ALK stratum; monitor lipids, edema, CNS effects, and cardiac conduction.

COG ANBL0032/ANBL1531 trial evidence: dose-intensive induction plus ASCR plus RT plus Dinutuximab/GM-CSF/Isotretinoin maintenance significantly improved EFS and OS over isotretinoin alone and remains the high-risk standard. Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
nodes.regimenSummary: Intensive 3-Phase: Dose-Intensive Induction -> Tandem ASCR + RT -> Dinutuximab + GM-CSF + Isotretinoin

nodes.name: Relapsed Refractory Treatment
nodes.title: Relapsed / Refractory Neuroblastoma: Chemoimmunotherapy or MIBG or ALK Therapy
nodes.description: Salvage therapy for relapsed or refractory neuroblastoma: chemoimmunotherapy backbone with MIBG and ALK-directed alternatives by avidity and genotype.
bullets: Chemoimmunotherapy backbone (D-I/T) per COG ANBL1221: Dinutuximab 17.5 mg/m2/d IV days 2-5 plus Irinotecan 50 mg/m2/d IV days 1-5 plus Temozolomide 100-150 mg/m2/d PO days 1-5 every 21-28 days with GM-CSF support; give cefixime or cefpodoxime prophylaxis for irinotecan-associated diarrhea, antiemetics, and opioid premedication for Dinutuximab pain.

131I-MIBG therapy for MIBG-avid relapsed disease: weight-based 131I-MIBG (typically 12-18 mCi/kg) with potassium iodide thyroid blockade, stem-cell availability, and isolation precautions; combine with myeloablative chemotherapy and ASCR at experienced centers for isolated MIBG-persistent sites.

Targeted ALK inhibitor Lorlatinib 95 mg/m2 PO once daily for ALK-mutant or ALK-amplified tumors (F1174, R1275, F1245 hotspot mutations or amplification by NGS/FISH); continue until progression; monitor hyperlipidemia, weight gain, peripheral edema, CNS effects, and AV block with ECG and lipid panels.

COG ANBL1221 trial evidence: Dinutuximab plus Irinotecan plus Temozolomide produced superior objective response rates versus Temozolomide plus Irinotecan alone in relapsed/refractory neuroblastoma and is the preferred salvage backbone; re-biopsy and repeat MYCN/ALK testing at relapse because clonal evolution is common.

Re-stage with MIBG or FDG-PET, bilateral marrow, urine HVA/VMA, and cross-sectional imaging every 2-3 cycles; prioritize clinical trial enrollment (anti-GD2 combinations, ALK inhibitors, CAR-T) at every relapse step. Physician decides; dose engine calculates patient-specific doses.
